notes.text: Nick Suzuki is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:10 together, down from 59% with Suzuki.
Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mike Matheson is out two weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, up from 6% last season.
Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Gavin McKenna has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews.
Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Dakota Mermis has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Max Domi is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season.
Chris Tanev returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Vinni Lettieri was added to the roster on Oct 19 and has played beside Colton Sissons and Gavin McKenna.
Dakota Mermis was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Maple Leafs go in tied for fourth in the Atlantic with 18 points, 2 points behind the Canadiens, second. A regulation win for the Maple Leafs would pull them level with the Canadiens. The Canadiens have two games in hand.

TOR.head: A slightly uphill night for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Toronto will be without Marchenko. Then again, Toronto has home-ice advantage, and Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Maple Leafs’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

MTL.head: The Canadiens have a slight edge
MTL.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Toronto will be without Marchenko. Then again, Toronto has home-ice advantage, and Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Maple Leafs can still swing it if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Canadiens are on a heater
paras: The Canadiens already played in Toronto once this season and left with a 3-2 win on Sep 29. The Maple Leafs (8-6-2) beat Vancouver 4-2 on Oct 31. The Canadiens are on a tear, five straight wins. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Canadiens second (fifth in the NHL) and the Maple Leafs sixth (tied for eighth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Canadiens’ record (.714) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.567), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Maple Leafs’ (.562 on chances worth .502), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Canadiens (32nd) and the Maple Leafs (31st) both take more penalties than they draw. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th). The Maple Leafs, by contrast, have had shaky goaltending (30th). They also get their shots through better than anyone (1st). Toronto has scored 3.75 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Habs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. Beyond that, the Canadiens wait for good looks, but the Maple Leafs settle for hopeful ones.

Lane Hutson (3 G / 10 A / 13 P in 14 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, and Cole Caufield (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Auston Matthews (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 16 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, with six goals in ten games against Montréal since 2023-24. William Nylander (10 G / 11 A / 21 P in 16 GP) is next in line.

Jacob Fowler (7-1-0 / .932 SV% in 8 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and will likely start. Toronto has two options in net: Sergei Bobrovsky (3-5-2 / .885 SV% in 10 GS) and Anthony Stolarz (5-1-0 / .910 SV% in 6 GS). Bobrovsky has started six of their last ten games, but Stolarz got the last one on Oct 31. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Canadiens usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Mike Matheson, and have been without Nick Suzuki, Samuel Montembeault and Ivan Demidov for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.

The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko, have been without Nick Blankenburg and John Tavares for several games, and have had to make do without Max Domi all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Islanders are missing more right now.
Jack Roslovic has a point in six straight games.
Auston Matthews has a point in four straight games.
